definitions.explanation: Something that has gone missing or been lost. A somewhat old-fashioned or literary word, still used in everyday speech in some regions and in certain set phrases.

examples.japanese: {失|う}せ{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}つかった→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧。
{失|う}せ{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}て→出る：00513_deru⟧こない。
examples.english: The missing item hasn't turned up.

examples.japanese: {失|う}せ{物|もの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{守|まも}り→お守り：05955_omamori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}ったら→買う：00489_kau⟧、なくした⟦{鍵|かぎ}→鍵：02189_kagi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}つかった→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧。
examples.english: After I bought a charm for finding lost things, I found the keys I had lost.

notes:
Has a slightly old-fashioned or traditional flavor. Particularly associated with prayers and charms at shrines for recovering lost items ({失|う}せ{物|もの}{探|さが}し). The verb ⟦{失|う}せる→失せる：12175_useru⟧ means to vanish or disappear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {失|う}せ{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}つかる→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧: a lost item is found
- {失|う}せ{物|もの}⟦{探|さが}し→探す：00493_sagasu⟧: searching for a lost item
- {失|う}せ{物|もの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{守|まも}り→お守り：05955_omamori⟧: charm for finding lost things
- {失|う}せ{物|もの}{封|ふう}じ: ritual to find lost items

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{落|お}とし{物|もの}→落とし物：08450_otoshimono⟧: dropped item, lost property — the standard modern term used at police stations and lost-and-found counters
- ⟦{忘|わす}れ{物|もの}→忘れ物：01758_wasuremono⟧: forgotten item — something left behind accidentally, especially on trains or at shops
- ⟦{紛失物|ふんしつぶつ}→紛失物：24102_funshitsubutsu⟧: lost property — formal/official term used in legal or administrative contexts
